title: Der goldene Schlüssel
source: Brüder Grimm, Kinder- und Hausmärchen, Band 2, 7. Auflage (Ausgabe letzter Hand), Dieterich, Göttingen 1857, KHM 200. Text from Wikisource („Der goldene Schlüssel (1857)“, twice proofread against the original). Fresh translation made directly from the German; 1857 spelling preserved exactly.
about: KHM 200 is the last piece in the whole collection, and one of the shortest things in it: a poor boy sent out for firewood in deep snow scrapes the ground clear to build himself a fire, turns up a small golden key, digs where he found it, and brings out an iron casket to match. He hunts for the keyhole, finds one almost too small to see, and turns the key once — and there the tale stops, on a sentence saying that we must wait until he has it fully unlocked and the lid up before we find out what lay inside. The stopping point is the point; nothing is missing.

sentences.t: Zur Winterszeit, als einmal ein tiefer Schnee lag, mußte ein armer Junge hinausgehen und Holz auf einem Schlitten holen.
sentences.l: In the winter time, when once a deep snow lay, a poor boy had to go out and fetch wood on a sled.
sentences.i: In the winter season, at a time when deep snow lay on the ground, a poor boy had to go out and fetch wood on a sledge.
sentences.n: die Winterszeit is the older compound for the winter season (Winter + linking ‑s‑ + Zeit). Of snow, German says it “lies” — ein tiefer Schnee lag — where English would say it lay on the ground. “mußte” is the 1857 spelling of musste.

sentences.t: Wie er es nun zusammengesucht und aufgeladen hatte, wollte er, weil er so erfroren war, noch nicht nach Haus gehen, sondern erst Feuer anmachen und sich ein bischen wärmen.
sentences.l: When he had now gathered it together and loaded it up, he did not want, because he was so frozen through, to go home yet, but first to make a fire and warm himself a little.
sentences.i: When he had gathered it all together and loaded it up, he did not want to go home yet, being so frozen through, but to make a fire first and warm himself a little.
sentences.n: “wie” at the head of a clause is temporal here — when, as — not the modern “how”. Two separable verbs: zusammensuchen (to gather together) and aufladen (to load up); in the participles the particle stays welded to the front. “bischen” is the 1857 spelling of bißchen.

sentences.t: Da scharrte er den Schnee weg, und wie er so den Erdboden aufräumte, fand er einen kleinen goldenen Schlüssel.
sentences.l: Then he scraped the snow away, and as he was so clearing the ground, he found a little golden key.
sentences.i: So he scraped the snow away, and while he was clearing the bare ground like that, he found a small golden key.
sentences.n: wegscharren is separable — scharrte … weg, with the particle thrown to the end of the clause. aufräumen is to clear or tidy; what he is clearing here is the frozen earth itself, not a room.

sentences.t: Nun glaubte er wo der Schlüssel wäre, müßte auch das Schloß dazu sein, grub in der Erde und fand ein eisernes Kästchen.
sentences.l: Now he thought, where the key was, the lock belonging to it must be there too, dug in the earth, and found an iron little box.
sentences.i: Now he reasoned that where the key was, the lock that went with it must be there too; so he dug in the earth and found a little iron box.
sentences.n: “wäre” and “müßte” are subjunctive — the sentence reports the boy’s reasoning without quoting him, and German marks that with the verb form rather than with “he thought that”. “das Schloß dazu” = the lock belonging to it; dazu points back to the key. das Schloß here is a lock, not a castle, though the corpus more often meets the other sense.

sentences.t: „Wenn der Schlüssel nur paßt!“ dachte er, „es sind gewiß kostbare Sachen in dem Kästchen.“
sentences.l: “If only the key fits!” he thought, “there are surely precious things in the little box.”
sentences.i: “If only the key fits!” he thought; “there must be precious things in that little box.”
sentences.n: “Wenn … nur” with a plain present verb and no main clause is a wish — if only. “gewiß” and “paßt” are the 1857 spellings of gewiss and passt.

sentences.t: Er suchte, aber es war kein Schlüsselloch da, endlich entdeckte er eins, aber so klein daß man es kaum sehen konnte.
sentences.l: He searched, but there was no keyhole there, at last he discovered one, but so small that one could hardly see it.
sentences.i: He searched, but there was no keyhole to be found; at last he discovered one, but so small that it could scarcely be made out.
sentences.n: “es war … da” — the da is the “there” of existence, as in da sein, to be there at all. “eins” stands in for the neuter das Schlüsselloch: he discovered one. “daß” is the 1857 spelling of dass.

sentences.t: Er probierte und der Schlüssel paßte glücklich.
sentences.l: He tried it and the key fitted luckily.
sentences.i: He tried it, and as luck would have it the key fitted.
sentences.n: “glücklich” here is the older adverbial sense — luckily, as good fortune had it — not “happily” of mood.

sentences.t: Da drehte er einmal herum, und nun müssen wir warten bis er vollends aufgeschlossen und den Deckel aufgemacht hat, dann werden wir erfahren was für wunderbare Sachen in dem Kästchen lagen.
sentences.l: Then he turned it once round, and now we must wait until he has fully unlocked it and has opened the lid, then we shall learn what wonderful things were lying in the little box.
sentences.i: Then he gave it one turn — and now we must wait until he has finished unlocking it and lifted the lid; then we shall find out what wonderful things were lying in that little box.
sentences.n: The tale ends here, and ends on purpose: this is the closing piece of the 1857 collection, and the lid is never lifted. “nun müssen wir warten” puts teller and listener in the same room together, still waiting. “was für” is the standard German frame for what sort of, what kind of. The past tense of “lagen” at the very end is the odd touch — the contents are spoken of as already past, though the box has not been opened.

glossary.drehte: drehen — turned (3rd sg. past; here herumdrehen, drehte … herum, gave it a turn)
glossary.eins: eins — one (neuter pronoun standing in for a preceding neuter noun)
glossary.entdeckte: entdecken — discovered, caught sight of (3rd sg. past; here of finding the keyhole)
glossary.herum: herum — round, around (separable particle: herumdrehen, to turn round)
glossary.junge: der Junge — boy (masc. noun; not the adjective jung, young)
glossary.schloß: das Schloß — lock (1857 spelling of Schloss; the same spelling also means ‘castle’)
